audit.whatIsWrong: win[0] and win[3] read Skill while the whys under them describe Teemo winning outright — whys[0] says 'you concede and farm at max Q range', whys[3] says 'he chips you between every failed step-in'.
audit.why: Packet chart gives Teemo Level 1 and Levels 4-5, and the Emerald+ win rate is 39.29%. Blinding Dart is a flat 7s at every rank against a champion whose damage is basic attacks, and Graves has no dash at all until level 3.
audit.corrected: win[0] and win[3] flipped to Teemo in both layers. Left win[1] and win[2] as Teemo to stay consistent with the already-audited Teemo side of the mirror, which set exactly those two.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every full-layer phase why was generic Graves boilerplate — 'four shells of buckshot win any level-1 face-off' sitting under a stage this page concedes, and 'crit scalers pass you' in a matchup with no crit scaler on either side.
audit.why: The stage drivers here are Blinding Dart's flat 7s (it never gets shorter, so it does not open up as the game goes on), Toxic Shot's on-hit poison, Move Quick, and the Noxious Trap field that eventually denies Graves any path into his own range.
audit.corrected: All seven whys rewritten to the abilities that actually decide each stage.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page's core plan is to 'smoke-blind him' — spikes[0], mid, whys[2] and wants.you[0] all have Teemo blinded inside Smoke Screen so his auto and Q miss. Graves has no blind.
audit.why: Graves W: 'creates a cloud of smoke that reduces sight range. Enemies caught in the initial impact are dealt magic damage and have their Move Speed reduced briefly.' The Teemo-side audit corrected the identical claim from his perspective: the smoke is a fog you should not fight blind inside, not a counter-blind.
audit.corrected: Reworded everywhere to the real effect — impact slow plus sight-range cut — which is still the reason the smoke pins him for the burst.

audit.whatIsWrong: Collateral Damage is called a 'wall escape' in whys[4], spikes[1] and mid.
audit.why: Graves R deals damage to the first champion hit and explodes in a cone. It has no displacement and does not move Graves — against a champion whose entire plan is kiting you, believing your ultimate is an escape is how you die at the end of a failed engage.
audit.corrected: Restated as a finisher in all three places.

audit.whatIsWrong: Move Quick's break condition and Guerrilla Warfare's invisibility never appear.
audit.why: Teemo W: 'passively increasing his Move Speed until he is struck by an enemy champion or turret.' One connected shell removes the passive speed — the single thing that makes chasing him viable. Teemo passive: 'If he's in brush, Teemo can enter and maintain his Invisibility while moving', which is why brush facechecks lose games in this lane.

edits.before: Teemo's Q blind is the entire problem: it lands on your point-blank shell spread and your autos do nothing, while your whole kit is built around being in his face. At level 1 you have one ability, no E dash yet, and short shell range, so just last-hit at the tip of your Q and eat the poison rather than walk into a free blind-and-kite. Every failed step-up costs you HP his Move Quick passive guarantees you can't trade back, since he move-speeds out of range before your spread connects.
edits.after: Teemo's Q blind is the entire problem: a flat 7 seconds at every rank, it lands on your point-blank shell spread and your autos do nothing, while your whole kit is built around being in his face. At level 1 you have one ability, no E dash, and short shell range, so last-hit at the tip of your Q rather than walk into a free blind-and-kite. One thing pays: Move Quick's passive speed drops the moment a champion strikes him, so one connected shell takes the kite away. Never facecheck brush — Guerrilla Warfare keeps him invisible while he moves in it.

edits.before: Levels 2-3 are your one real opening: lob W (Smoke Screen) onto Teemo so his auto and Q are blinded while he's standing in the cloud, E in, and dump the shell spread + Q before he walks out of it. The hard truth is his Q blind is up more often than your engage, so you only fully commit when it's on cooldown — bait it with a fake step-up first. At 6 your R is a no-dash nuke and a wall escape, so a blind-down E-Q-R is your cleanest kill, but a Q-ready Teemo just zeroes the spread and kites away.
edits.after: Levels 2-3 are your one real opening: lob W (Smoke Screen) onto Teemo so the impact slow and the sight-range cut pin him in the cloud, E in, and dump the shell spread + Q before he walks out. Smoke Screen does not blind — nothing you own makes his attacks miss. His dart is a flat 7 seconds, up more often than your engage, so only fully commit when it is down; bait it with a fake step-up first. At 6 the R is a nuke, not an escape, so a blind-down E-Q-R is your cleanest kill, while a Q-ready Teemo zeroes the spread.

notes: The page's entire game plan was 'smoke-blind him' — Graves has no blind, and the Teemo-side audit already corrected the same claim from the other direction, so the two pages now agree. Second fabrication removed: Collateral Damage as a wall escape, in three places. Best concrete addition: Blinding Dart is a FLAT 7 seconds at every rank, so unlike most matchup-defining cooldowns it never opens up as the game goes on — and Move Quick's passive speed breaks the instant a champion strikes him, which is the one lever Graves has against the kite. I left win[1] and win[2] as Teemo rather than moving them to the packet's Skill, because the Teemo-side audit set exactly those two and I would rather not fight the mirror.
